purpose: Determine whether the categorical calibration ceiling is specific to binary mismatch + Spearman or persists under an alternative association statistic applied to the identical simulated binary states and tree geometries.
source_scope: Nominal-categorical novel systems from the frozen 683-system known-truth simulation family; no real trait outcomes.

estimators.primary_existing: Spearman correlation between patristic distance and 0/1 mismatch.
estimators.alternative: Standardized mean separation contrast: (mean patristic distance among mismatch pairs - mean distance among match pairs) / SD of all pairwise patristic distances.

generator: Identical frozen OU latent process followed by threshold at zero; same lambda grid, seeds, pilot replicates and tree geometries.
calibration_target_rule: For each estimator separately, define its benchmark as the median alternative-statistic value generated at the lambda that targets Spearman rho=0.15 on a large balanced reference tree fixed before system analysis. Do not tune benchmark per system.
primary_comparison: Fraction of categorical systems with a calibration bracket under Spearman versus the alternative statistic.
secondary: Known-truth recovery conditional on calibration for the alternative statistic using analogous relative benchmark error and directional criteria frozen after reference-tree calibration but before real-system alternative results.
interpretation: If the alternative removes much of the no-bracket ceiling, the bottleneck is estimator-specific. If not, the limitation is more fundamentally tied to binary representation and realized tree geometry.
